questions.prompt: What is the key advantage of a computed property over a method for derived values?

options.text: It runs on the server
It is cached and only re-evaluates when a reactive dependency changes
It can perform side effects safely
It never needs to be read

questions.explanation: A computed caches its result based on its dependencies and re-runs only when one of them changes; a method runs every time it is called.

questions.prompt: When does a computed property re-run its getter?

options.text: On every render, always
Only when one of its reactive dependencies changes
Once, and never again
Every 100 milliseconds

questions.explanation: Vue tracks which reactive values the getter reads and re-evaluates only when one of those dependencies changes.

questions.prompt: How do you make a computed property writable?

options.text: You can't — computed is always read-only
Pass computed() an object with get and set functions
Add a second argument true
Wrap it in reactive()

questions.explanation: computed({ get, set }) creates a writable computed; assigning to its .value calls the setter.

questions.prompt: A computed getter should be free of ______ effects — it should only derive and return a value. (one word)
questions.explanation: Computed getters must be side-effect-free; mutating other state or fetching data belongs in a watcher, not a getter.

questions.prompt: Which are good reasons to use a computed property? Select all that apply.

options.text: To keep the template clean by naming a derived value
To cache an expensive calculation over reactive data
To run a fetch request each time it's read
To derive a value from other reactive state

questions.explanation: Computed properties name and cache derived values from reactive state. They must not perform side effects like fetching data.

questions.prompt: You call a computed property's value 10 times without changing its dependencies. How many times does the getter actually run?

options.text: 10 times
Once (the result is cached)
Zero times
It depends on the browser

questions.explanation: The getter runs once and the cached result is reused until a dependency changes.
